drug_class: Dopamine agonist (a medicine that mimics a brain chemical called dopamine)
purpose: Rotigotine is used to treat Parkinson's disease, helping to reduce symptoms like tremors, stiffness, and slow movement. It is also used to treat a condition called Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS), which causes uncomfortable sensations and an urge to move your legs, especially at night. It helps improve your ability to move and sleep more comfortably.
how_it_works: Your brain uses a chemical called dopamine to help control smooth, coordinated movement. In Parkinson's disease, the brain doesn't make enough dopamine. Rotigotine acts like dopamine in your brain, filling in for the missing chemical and helping your body move more normally. For Restless Legs Syndrome, it calms the nerve signals that cause those uncomfortable sensations in your legs.
common_side_effects: The patch can cause skin redness, itching, or irritation where you apply it. You may also feel nauseous, dizzy, or sleepy. Some people notice swelling in the legs, headache, or increased sweating. It can sometimes cause sudden sleepiness during the day, so be careful when driving.
warnings: Do not stop using this patch suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as it can cause serious withdrawal symptoms. This medicine can cause compulsive behaviors in some people, such as gambling, overeating, or increased sexual urges — tell your doctor right away if this happens. It may lower your blood pressure when you stand up, causing dizziness or fainting. Avoid exposing the patch to direct heat like heating pads or saunas, as it can release too much medicine too quickly. Tell your doctor if you have any mental health conditions, as it can rarely cause hallucinations or confusion.
typical_dosing: Rotigotine comes as a patch that you wear on your skin and change once every 24 hours. For Parkinson's disease, you usually start with a low dose patch (2 mg per 24 hours) and your doctor may slowly increase it over several weeks up to the dose that works best for you. For Restless Legs Syndrome, the starting dose is typically 1 mg per 24 hours, and it may be increased if needed. Always apply the patch to clean, dry, hairless skin and rotate the spot each day to avoid irritation.
